claim: The attacker of Mac Malware Steals Crypto stole credentials.
quote:
Steals saved usernames and passwords in Chrome
Steals saved credit card credentials in Chrome
locator: PDF p. 2 (web page, unpaginated), behaviour rundown
issue: Adversarial read: the report describes the malware's capability ('CookieMiner'), not a counted set of victims; it also says the cookies are uploaded 'to a remote' server (PDF p. 3), so theft, not mere access, is reported. Holds.

claim: It mined cryptocurrency on the victims' machines, hijacking them, so it impeded systems.
quote: Mines cryptocurrency on the victim’s machine
locator: PDF p. 2 (web page, unpaginated), behaviour rundown
issue: 'Hijacking' and 'impeded' are the thesis's categorisation (ATT&CK Resource Hijacking under Impact, defined in Sect. 4.2), not the report's words; the report states the mining. The deduction is labelled as ours ('so it'), so the cite carries the fact, not the category.

claim: Table C.1 row: the report is the threat report the Mac Malware Steals Crypto flow cites and supports its c3 class (stole data and impeded systems).
quote:
This malware is capable of stealing browser cookies associated with mainstream
cryptocurrency exchanges and wallet service websites visited by the victims.
issue: The flow file cites this Unit 42 URL (mac-malware-steals-cryptocurrency-exchanges-cookies). The c3 'impeded' half rests on mining as resource hijacking (see U0946).
